correctness.rationale: The sharp surface-area equality conditions follow from a complete Gram-matrix reduction, Cauchy–Schwarz and the exact symmetric-polynomial maximum. Every barycentric orthonormal basis in dimension three is represented by an equilateral three-angle family. On three 120-degree angles, its degree-two quadratic signal aliases to a degree-one harmonic, and exact solvability is |delta|^2=2|eta|^2. Expanding the transverse projection identities gives the claimed invariant quartic with both implications, including degenerate coupling cases. A standalone SymPy checker verifies symbolic identities, an exact off-axis maximizer, eight boundary points and surface equality; 300 numerical reconstructions only support consistency.

originality.rationale: Kania explicitly leaves the general dimension-three prescribed-vertex restricted Schur-Horn classification open in Problem 6.1, giving only the principal-axis case in Theorem 5.5. The new invariant necessary-and-sufficient quartic covers every direction, reconstructs a solution, and yields previously untreated off-axis latitude circles on ellipsoids of revolution. Damm–Faßbender and Nicholus prove different weaker real hollowization statements, not equivalent to the full simultaneous real-orthogonal barycentric condition. Targeted public research-index and general literature searches located no equivalent complete criterion. Residual historical-priority risk remains.

value.rationale: This resolves, for all real ellipsoids and all boundary points in dimension three, the first higher-dimensional case of Kania’s explicit Problem 6.1. It gives a coordinate-free exact decision polynomial plus a constructive maximizing box, with the new aspect-ratio-independent non-principal latitude circles |y·v|=1/3 for ellipsoids of revolution. This structural classification is neither a textbook corollary nor an arbitrary parameter slice, and directly answers a motivated geometric extremal problem.
